title: Emergency tenant rehome and hybrid fallback sequencing
creator: Ananya Patel
description: Summary: During a partial region outage we observed a subset of tenants with KV-shard affinity become stranded on cold hosts after an orchestrator mis-scheduled evac events. This ticket coordinates an emergency rehome flow for impacted tenants, a hybrid fallback sequencing (hosted -> dedicated-compatible fallback -> degraded local serving), required circuit-breakers, and customer communications. Goals: 1) restore request routing for affected tenants within SLO targets, 2) avoid KV cache loss and double-write corruption, 3) minimize overall blast radius and cost, 4) provide a repeatable, operator-safe playbook for future incidents. Scope: hosted + dedicated topologies. Excludes full private on-prem upgrades, but includes guidance for VPC customers that opt into platform-managed failover. Key constraints: we cannot sync cold KV snapshots synchronously for large tenants without risking 2-3x latency spikes; any rehome must pre-warm KV caches and verify shard ownership. Approach: - Calculate impacted tenant list using shard-provenance logs and per-tenant last-successful-heartbeat. - For high-priority tenants (SLA customers or high-traffic), perform prefill: provision target host warm slab, replay recent KV deltas (bounded to last 5 minutes) into staging cache, run consistency check. - Use a traffic-steering policy that moves 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2-minute windows with success gates (99.5% request success, 95th latency < configured SLO). - Implement a hybrid fallback route: if hosted variant fails capacity checks, route through dedicated-compatible pool with tokenized throttles; fallback to local degraded path (stateless best-effort) only if both prior tiers fail. - Introduce temporary per-tenant circuit breaker to avoid cascading retries across regions. - Instrument short-lived feature flags and canary probes (synthetic requests) for each rehome step. Acceptance criteria: impacted tenants have <5 minutes to first success, end-to-end latency within SLO for 95% of requests during roll, no data-loss or inconsistent KV state detected post-rehome, and a customer-facing incident summary sent within 90 minutes of remediation start. Links: runbook draft https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/tenant-rehome-playbook, incident dashboard https://dash.redwood.ai/incident/2026-03-10-zh, proposed PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1427
